note: Listen to anything. Transmit only where your license allows; in a real emergency, FCC rules (for example 47 CFR 97.403 for amateur radio) allow any means of radio communication to call for help when life or property is in immediate danger.

groups.name: FRS / GMRS (blister-pack walkie-talkies)
groups.license: FRS: none (2 W, 0.5 W on 8–14). GMRS: FCC license, no exam, covers your family (up to 5 W on 1–7, 50 W on 15–22).

channels.use: Widely used GMRS emergency/travel channel (often with 141.3 Hz tone)

groups.name: MURS (license-free VHF, 2 W)
groups.license: None. Better range than FRS outdoors.

groups.name: NOAA Weather Radio (listen only)
groups.license: Receive only. Continuous forecasts and alerts; find your local transmitter's frequency by scanning.

groups.name: Marine VHF
groups.license: For use on the water. Listening on land is fine.

groups.name: Amateur (ham) radio
groups.license: Transmitting needs an FCC amateur license (Technician exam: 35 questions). Study pool in Content → Field manuals → Grid-down essentials.
